hypothesis: Candidate-level CP-SAT propagation over the exhaustive radius-3 all-row neighborhood will solve the finite compatibility-cover problem more effectively than the capped Python DFS and may return a validator-accepted scope-111 DTS.
rationale: The prior all-row enumeration found 48,600 valid row masks and reached depth 5 before a 5,000,000-node DFS cap. Encoding each row mask as a Boolean candidate, requiring exactly one candidate per baseline row, and constraining each difference to appear at most once preserves the finite neighborhood exactly while exposing global propagation to CP-SAT.
expected_information_gain: Tests whether the coordinated-repair neighborhood contains a target assignment and whether candidate-level exact-cover propagation, rather than integer mark search or naive DFS, can expose it within a bounded Linux run.
method: Enumerate all 7^5 coordinate perturbations with radius 3 around each published row, retain valid scope<=111 Golomb rows, deduplicate by difference mask, and solve the resulting Boolean exact-cover model under WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04 Python 3.14 with OR-Tools 9.15.6755, eight workers, seed 20260827, and a 120-second timeout. Independently validate any selected seven rows with verify_dts.verify.
metric: CP-SAT status, candidate-pool cardinality, elapsed time, selected rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A FEASIBLE or OPTIMAL selected cover accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; UNKNOWN is solver evidence only and does not imply the finite neighborhood or global problem is infeasible.

configuration.candidate_generation: exhaustive 7^5 perturbations per row, mask deduplication
cover_constraints: at most one selected candidate per difference 1..111

kill_condition: Stop after a validator-valid complete assignment or after 120 seconds; preserve UNKNOWN as solver evidence and do not expand the neighborhood during this experiment.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if selected cover is complete and validator-valid

previous_best_comparison.previous_neighborhood: 48,600 valid masks; Python DFS cap at depth 5
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: new information from exact-cover propagation or a validator-valid witness

interpretation: Candidate-level CP-SAT exact-cover propagation over all 48,100 valid radius-3 row masks returned UNKNOWN after 121.657 seconds with no assignment or bound. The finite neighborhood remains unresolved; UNKNOWN is not infeasibility or a DTS result.
what_was_learned: The candidate-level decomposition preserves a substantial finite search space but does not solve it within the tested short budget. Another solver on the same encoding would be low-value unless it provides a materially different proof/propagation capability; the next work should examine structural factorization or a stronger SAT encoding.
recommended_next_action: If a witness is found, freeze and escalate through independent/adversarial verification; otherwise stop this radius-3 neighborhood family and require a broader structural hypothesis.
repetition_justification: This changes the search representation from Python DFS over row masks to a Boolean exact-cover CP-SAT model while keeping the same exhaustive radius-3 candidate set and frozen DTS contract. It is not a larger timeout of the prior implementation.
